questions.stem: To which kind of data store is data federation restricted?
options: NoSQL databases
Web services and SaaS applications
Relational databases
Data appliances
Enterprise applications
questions.explanation: Data federation works conceptually like data virtualization but is restricted to relational databases, whereas virtualization also reaches appliances, NoSQL, web services, SaaS and enterprise applications.

questions.stem: What does data virtualization create that data federation does not?
options: A unified data model
A physical copy of the data
An ETL pipeline
A backup of the source systems
An access control list
questions.explanation: A major difference is that data federation does not create a unified data model, whereas data virtualization does.

questions.stem: The relationship between data federation and data virtualization is compared to the relationship between which pair?
options: Data warehouse and data mart
OLTP and OLAP
Data mining and data science
Encryption and encoding
Data lake and data swamp
questions.explanation: The relationship between data federation and data virtualization is likened to that between data mining and data science: the same idea, but one is the broader discipline.

questions.stem: Why do data federation and data virtualization require no additional storage?
options: Because they compress the source data heavily
Because they hold only a virtual copy rather than a separate copy of the data
Because they delete data after each query
Because they store data in the cloud rather than on-premises
Because they only ever read summary tables
questions.explanation: As a virtual copy, there is no cost for a separate copy of the data, so no additional storage is required.

questions.stem: Why is data federation described as low risk compared with a data warehouse or data lake?
options: Because it applies stronger encryption
Because it never allows write access
Because it is not hosting a data copy, so there is no chance of missing any data
Because it runs only on relational databases
Because it caches every query result
questions.explanation: Unlike warehouses or lakes where data is physically moved, federation hosts no copy, so there is no chance of missing any data.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a listed drawback shared by data federation and data virtualization?
options: Data must be physically moved through ETL
Users must learn a different query language for each source
Historical data is not maintained
A separate storage copy is required
Only one data store can be accessed at a time
questions.explanation: Because no copy of the data is hosted, history data is also not maintained; the other options contradict the listed benefits.

questions.stem: How do data federation and data virtualization make querying easier for users?
options: By generating dashboards automatically
By letting users write in one language while a wrapper talks to all connected systems
By replicating all data into a single relational database
By limiting queries to a single source at a time
By pre-computing every possible aggregate
questions.explanation: Users do not have to write queries in different languages; they write in one language and the tool creates a wrapper to talk to all the connected systems.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed as a shared behaviour of data federation and data virtualization?
options: Single access point
User access management in one place
No data movement
Complete historical copies of source data
Data quality issues identified from a single point
questions.explanation: Complete historical copies belong to data consolidation; federation and virtualization host no copy and therefore keep no history.

questions.stem: Why do data federation and data virtualization need dedicated involvement from data stewards and functional consultants?
options: Because functional knowledge of the connected sources is required
Because they must approve every ETL job
Because the tools cannot connect without manual scripting
Because they must maintain the historical archive
Because relational databases require licences
questions.explanation: Functional knowledge is a listed drawback: these approaches seek dedicated involvement by data stewards and functional consultants.

questions.stem: Alongside which data store are data federation and data virtualization best suited?
options: A data swamp
A message queue
A spreadsheet
A data warehouse in place
A scraping tool
questions.explanation: Both are best suited alongside a data warehouse in place, which provides the history they do not keep.
